transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2027-03-05 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Rachel Kim (Redwood AE), Daniel Ortiz (Redwood SE), Priya Shah (Mediva Head of Security), Liam O'Connor (CISO), Mateo Ruiz (Eng Manager)

[00:00] Rachel (Redwood): hey everyone thanks for joining, hope this time works. quick agenda — go over data residency and region pinning, talk through our hosted vs private options, and cover audit logs and encryption questions.
[00:18] Priya (Mediva): yep thanks, we've got about 45 minutes. main ask up front: all customer data for EU patients must remain in EU regions, we need to avoid cross-border processing unless explicitly approved by legal.
[00:34] Daniel (Redwood SE): absolutely, that's a common req. we support region pinning so requests from EU can be routed to eu-west clusters; also private deployments run entirely inside your VPC if needed.
[00:50] Liam (Mediva): can you clarify what you mean by "region pinning"? is that per-tenant, per-route, or per-request?
[01:05] Rachel: good question. we offer policy-based routing — you can pin at the tenant level (all traffic stays in region), or route by model/route. per-request pinning works too using metadata headers but that requires org configs.
[01:22] Mateo (Mediva): any chance of accidental fallbacks to us-east if eu capacity is saturated? that's our biggest concern.
[01:36] Daniel: we have configurable fallbacks. for strict EU-only there is a hard pin option with no cross-border fallback; for lower SLOs you can allow "same-tenant but failover within EU" or "fallback to compatible model in another region". we'll show config examples in the deep-dive.
[01:52] Priya: ok hard pin sounds necessary. also encryption — do you support customer-managed keys (CMK) via KMS? we need HSM-backed keys ideally.
[02:07] Rachel: yes, Redwood Private integrates with customer KMS/HSM and supports envelope encryption. for hosted we offer bring-your-own-key (BYOK) via supported KMS providers — you can rotate keys and we log key usage in audit logs.
[02:22] Liam: are keys stored in EU? we need key material to be in-region for GDPR concerns.
[02:31] Daniel: for private deployments keys stay in your KMS inside your VPC/region. for hosted BYOK we work with partners to provision keys in the required cloud region — we'll include region mapping in the docs. small caveat: some KMS providers replicate metadata globally for management tasks but we can document that.
[02:49] Priya: ok, please document any potential metadata flows.
[02:55] Rachel: noted. next on sub-processors: Mediva asked about third-party cloud or logging providers. we maintain a sub-processor list and notify customers for changes; we also offer a sub-processor audit on request.
[03:10] Mateo: do you use any US-based analytics for telemetry? that could trigger cross-border issues.
[03:18] Daniel: telemetry is configurable — you can forward metrics to your own monitoring endpoints in EU, or we can obfuscate PII before forwarding. some infra-level metrics are collected for platform health but we can limit retention and region.
[03:35] Priya: audit logs — retention and tamper-evidence? we need immutable logs for 7 years and access controls.
[03:44] Rachel: audit logs are stored with tamper-evidence options; for Private you control the storage backend and retention. For hosted customers we offer export to your S3/GCS with server-side encryption and object lock options for immutability.
[04:02] Liam: do you provide proof of integrity (hashing, chain of custody)?
[04:08] Daniel: yes we include digest hashes and can provide signed log bundles for audits. this is part of our enterprise package.
[04:20] Priya: SOC 2 and ISO — do you have Type II and ISO 27001 certificates?
[04:27] Rachel: we are SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 certified; i'll share the certs and the attestation report after this call.
[04:36] Mateo: great. also curious about network egress — if we do EU-hosted, are sub processors in US still called for model hosting?
[04:46] Daniel: for our curated open-model catalog, model weights may be stored in regional caches. we can ensure weights are only provisioned in EU if required, but some third-party vendors might require cross-region storage. we'll flag those models in the catalog.
[05:02] Priya: can you provide a list of models that are EU-resident guaranteed?
[05:08] Rachel: yes we'll provide a model residency matrix.
[05:11] Mateo: about private deployment options — VPC vs on-prem — what's the feature parity and maintenance expectations?
[05:21] Daniel: VPC private deployment gives control over networking, KMS, and storage while we manage the control plane; on-prem gives full isolation and we provide an air-gapped bundle if needed. feature parity is close but some hosted analytics may be absent on on-prem by default.
[05:38] Liam: what's the timeline for an on-prem deployment POC?
[05:42] Rachel: typical POC for VPC is 4-6 weeks; on-prem is 6-12 weeks depending on approvals.
[05:49] Priya: any sub-processor changes require 30-day notice?
[05:55] Rachel: our standard DPA includes 30-day notice for material changes to sub-processors; for high-risk changes we can negotiate additional notice.
[06:03] Mateo: ok good. one more: data subject access requests — relevant logs and data export, how fast can you support that?
[06:12] Daniel: we can run exports and provide a sanitized bundle; response SLA depends on plan but enterprise typically has a 72-hour turnaround for packaged exports.
[06:23] Priya: that's acceptable.
[06:26] Rachel: wanted to touch briefly on RBAC and SSO — do you use SAML / OIDC?
[06:32] Daniel: we support SAML SSO, OIDC, SCIM provisioning, and fine-grained RBAC. roles can be limited per-team and per-route.
[06:41] Mateo: can we restrict who can change region-pin settings?
[06:46] Daniel: yes RBAC controls admin-level policies; we generally recommend a separate region-admin role.
[06:52] Liam: legal will want to see the DPA and sub-processor list, and security will want SOC2, ISO, and an architecture diagram with region pinning flow.
[07:02] Rachel: we'll package those. action items captured.
[07:06] Priya: one last nit: cross-border processing exceptions — can you add an approval workflow when an explicit fallback outside EU is needed?
[07:16] Daniel: we can implement an allowlist-based exception flow where legal approval triggers a temporary token allowing fallback. it's custom but doable — we'll scope in the technical deep-dive.
[07:29] Rachel: great. next steps recap: i'll send SOC2 + ISO certs, model residency matrix, sub-processor list, and the DPA. daniel will schedule the vpc/on-prem deep dive and include config examples for hard pin vs soft pin. customer to share final residency matrix and legal team availability.
[07:48] Liam: thanks all. talk soon.

End of transcript. Note: occasional transcription errors may exist (e.g., K V cache / kv cache, V P C spelled out), speaker labels may not align perfectly in export.
